split: The main 2004--2021 experiment contains 18,410/3,945/3,945 raw training/validation/test timestamps and 18,404/3,939/3,939 forecast targets after six-snapshot windows are constructed separately within each partition. The target-time ranges (UTC) are 2 January 2004 12:00--7 August 2016 06:00 for training, 9 August 2016 00:00--20 April 2019 12:00 for validation, and 22 April 2019 06:00--31 December 2021 18:00 for testing. These are forecast target times, not input-window start times. The 1992--2003 extension is used only in the supplementary rolling-origin evaluation.
main_boot: The main saved-run BiLSTM-Attention--XGBoost RMSE comparison uses a paired circular-block bootstrap with 28 consecutive six-hourly samples (7 days), 10,000 replicates and resampling seed 42. Blocks wrap around the full test series and are truncated to the original sample length; rainfall-subset masks are applied after resampling the complete timeline. The reported 95\% percentile intervals are pointwise and are conditional on the original single saved predictions, not five-seed mean scores. Five-seed sample standard deviations instead measure training-initialization variability on a fixed chronological split; they do not measure uncertainty in cross-year generalization.
rolling_design: We conducted a retrospective rolling-origin robustness evaluation using the extended 1992--2021 ERA5 archive. Expanding training periods were 1992--2007, 1992--2010, 1992--2013 and 1992--2016; their validation periods were 2008--2009, 2011--2012, 2014--2015 and 2017--2018, and their non-overlapping test periods were 2010--2012, 2013--2015, 2016--2018 and 2019--2021, respectively (F1--F4). F4$\prime$ instead trained on 2004--2016 and shared F4\textquotesingle s validation and test targets, isolating the addition of 1992--2003 training history within this protocol. The longest training history was 25 years; F1 and F2 used 16 and 19 years. Six models and five fixed seeds (42, 123, 7, 2024, 99) yielded 150 runs. The six models were XGBoost, Transformer, BiLSTM-Attention, BU-LSTM, BU-LSTM-Attention and Probabilistic BiLSTM-Attention; the plain BiLSTM control was not included.
rolling_processing: Scalers, Q95, month-by-hour climatology and AR(1) coefficients were estimated from each fold\textquotesingle s training data only. A training-only check of the original 11-candidate contemporaneous screening rule recovered the same seven predictors in every fold; training retained that fixed set. Windows did not cross partition boundaries. Architectures and hyperparameters were reused from the original study, without fold-specific retuning; recurrent models retained the 30-epoch cap and validation-based early stopping. This preserves temporal separation at the preprocessing and model-fitting stages but does not make model-design choices independent of these retrospectively selected periods.
rolling_boot: Rolling-origin RMSE comparisons used a paired non-circular moving-block bootstrap: 28 six-hourly samples (7 days), 5,000 replicates and resampling seed 42, with additional pooled checks at 56 and 120 samples (14 and 30 days). Blocks were sampled on the full chronological sequence before wet-subset masking; each replicate used $\lceil n/L\rceil$ complete blocks of length $L$, without truncating its final block. Common sampled indices were applied across compared forecasts and seeds; RMSE differences were calculated per seed and then averaged, rather than averaging predictions first. Pooled comparisons concatenated F1--F4 targets before scoring and can sample blocks across the short fold-boundary gaps. All intervals are pointwise 95\% percentile intervals without multiplicity adjustment. Paired seed-$t$ intervals for the history comparison separately describe training variability across five seeds (four degrees of freedom); neither interval combines both uncertainty sources.
results: Across the four rolling test periods, all six learning models retained positive RMSE skill relative to training-fitted month-by-hour climatology (0.077--0.125). AR(1) also had positive skill (0.031--0.055), whereas Persistence had negative skill in every period. XGBoost had the numerically lowest RMSE in F1--F3, and BiLSTM-Attention in F4; pairwise Kendall rank correlations among the six-model rankings ranged from 0.60 to 0.87. Only F1\textquotesingle s BiLSTM-Attention--XGBoost all-target interval clearly excluded zero among the four period-specific comparisons. These results do not identify a uniformly best model.
pooled: On the 17,508 pooled test targets, the mean seed-level RMSE difference (BiLSTM-Attention minus XGBoost) was $+0.00204$~mm\,h$^{-1}$. Its 7-day interval was $[+0.00007,+0.00398]$, its 14-day interval $[-0.00003,+0.00402]$, and its 30-day interval $[+0.00006,+0.00404]$~mm\,h$^{-1}$. The small all-target separation is therefore sensitive to block length. On the distinct wet subset ($\geq0.1$~mm\,h$^{-1}$; $n=3,610$), the difference was $+0.0093$~mm\,h$^{-1}$ with a 7-day interval of $[+0.0048,+0.0137]$~mm\,h$^{-1}$, supporting lower XGBoost RMSE within that subset rather than an overall superiority claim.
history: On matched F4/F4$\prime$ test targets, extending training from 13 to 25 years reduced the six learning models\textquotesingle{} mean all-target RMSE by approximately 0.4--2.3\%. Upper-tail gains were not uniform, and seed-$t$ and test-sample bootstrap intervals did not always agree; both are retained. Conditional 95\% Gaussian coverage across F1--F4 was 0.953--0.963 overall, but only 0.801--0.828 for wet targets and 0.473--0.592 for upper-tail targets. Under the fixed Q95 rule, every learning model\textquotesingle s mean CSI was lower than Persistence in each period. The coverage and fixed-event diagnostics use fold-specific training Q95, whereas the history comparison uses the common original-main Q95 $=0.574048$~mm\,h$^{-1}$ for upper-tail targets. Fixed-cutoff event scores are distinct from the validation-selected decisions reported elsewhere.
qualification: BiLSTM-Attention achieved the numerically lowest RMSE on the original test period, but its advantage over XGBoost was small and did not persist consistently across the rolling-origin evaluation.
limitations: The rolling-origin analysis is retrospective rather than a fully prospective or fully independent validation of model-design choices. The original training targets extended through 7 August 2016 and validation targets through 20 April 2019; these development data overlap the F1--F3 test years. F4 begins on 2 January 2019, so its early-2019 targets also overlap the original validation period; the original test targets begin only on 22 April 2019. The original test portion was not used for initial hyperparameter selection but had already informed the original model comparisons. Fold-specific fitting and preprocessing therefore do not remove development-stage overlap. Models were not retuned per fold; F1/F2 had only 16/19 training years. No ENSO-phase stratification, rolling plain-BiLSTM control or rolling Bernoulli--Gamma alternative was evaluated. Pooled bootstrap blocks can cross the 42-hour gaps between adjacent fold target sequences. These boundaries limit claims of temporal independence, attention-specific benefit and robustness to distributional formulation.
